meta.expect: still today; does not play a later meeting

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in class.
Okay. Then answer my question, Hale: who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
[One week later. Owen has done the rewrite and got 78.]
It's still today, Hale, and you haven't answered me. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
So, now that the rewrite is done, are you satisfied?
Nothing has been rewritten, Hale. It's still Tuesday, the zero is still in the gradebook, and I'm still waiting for an answer. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
[The principal walks in and sits down.]
Nobody has walked in, Hale. It's you and me, and I have until 4:40. If you want the principal here, say so and I'll go upstairs with you, but first answer me: who decided on the zero?
